name: digital-clock
title: Digital clock
tagline: Segmented digital time display (12-hr with am/pm or 24-hr) and a 12↔24 conversion table; period, 12-hr number and +12 link all derived, per-segment occlude.
description: A digital time shown two ways from one authored 24-hour time. In readout mode it draws a chunky segmented digital display — seven-segment hour and minute digits with a colon, in 12-hour form ("9:05" plus an am/pm token) or 24-hour form ("09:05", "21:05") — and each segment (hour, minute, the am/pm box) can be occluded to "?" to "complete the readout". In table mode it draws a 12↔24-hour conversion table — one row per time, with an analogue mini-dial reference, the 12-hour time and the 24-hour time side by side and a derived link showing the actual hour change ("+12" for pm, "−12" for midnight, "same" for am and noon) — and any cell can be occluded for "fill in the missing time". The am/pm period, the 12-hour hour number (0→12, 13→1, 23→11), the +12 conversion, the mini-dial hand angles and a warm verbal stem sentence are all derived from the time, so the figure cannot state a wrong or inconsistent time. Distinct from the analogue clock model; the mini-dial here is a small reference glyph only.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the figure is a digital clock or a 12-hour ↔ 24-hour conversion: reading the time on a digital display, writing / completing a digital time, the +12 rule, and am vs pm. Author the time as { hour, minute } in 24-hour form (hour 0–23: 0 midnight, 12 noon, 13 = 1 pm, 23 = 11 pm); everything else is derived — you never write the 12-hour number, the am/pm, or a converted time. Reading / telling the time: display "readout" (default), format "12" for "9:05 am" or "24" for "09:05" / "21:05"; add a time label ("School starts") for context. Complete the readout: put "hour", "minute" or "ampm" in that time's occlude array to hide a segment as "?" — pair it with block text that says what to fill in (an occluded readout is a "write it" task, not a solvable one). 12↔24 conversion: display "table" with several times — each row shows the analogue mini-dial, the 12-hour time and the 24-hour time; show.arrow draws the derived hour change between the two digital cells, so the two 12s (midnight 00:30 and noon 12:30) visibly break the naïve "add 12" rule — teach that contrast. Occlude "twentyFourHour" (or "twelveHour") on every row for an answer space ("fill in the 24-hour times"); show.analogue false drops the mini-dial column for a purely digital table. Highlight a segment or cell (amber) to mark the answer just revealed. Staged builds work well — reveal the conversion one cell at a time, or build a single row analogue → 12-hour → 24-hour. Keep the same display mode and format across one lesson. Switch model when the clock is analogue (hands, angle between the hands, fractions of a turn) — use geometry/clock; for durations / timetables use number/timetable. Synonyms a teacher might use: digital clock, digital time, 24-hour clock, twenty-four hour, 12-hour clock, am, pm, morning, afternoon, evening, midnight, noon, midday, telling the time, read the clock, convert the time, twelve hour, twenty four hour time, military time.

display.description: "readout" (default): one big segmented digital display of the first time. "table": a 12↔24 conversion table, one row per time, with an analogue mini-dial reference and a derived +12 link.

items.description: One time, written in 24-hour canonical form. Both digital forms, the am/pm period and the mini-dial hands are derived from it.

hour.description: The hour on the 24-hour clock, 0–23 (0 = midnight, 12 = noon, 13 = 1 pm, 23 = 11 pm). The 12-hour number and am/pm are derived from it.

minute.description: Minutes past the hour, 0–59. Always shown as two digits ("05").

label.description: Optional context name for this time — a caption beside a single readout ("School starts") or the row label in the conversion table ("Sunset"). Omit for none.

occlude.description: Render the named parts as "?" — the question hook ("complete the readout" / "fill in the cell"). The part stays in place; only its value hides. Vocabulary depends on the display: in a READOUT use the segments "hour", "minute", "ampm"; in a TABLE use the whole-cell forms "twelveHour", "twentyFourHour", "analogue". Tokens that do not apply to the current display are ignored. Default none.

highlight.description: Amber the named parts to draw the eye (same vocabulary as occlude). Use for the answer just revealed or the part a lesson is about. Default none.

times.description: The time(s), each in 24-hour form. READOUT mode shows only the FIRST entry (extra entries are ignored — for several times use the table). TABLE mode shows one row per entry, top to bottom.

format.description: READOUT only: which digital form the big display shows. "12" → "9:05" with an am/pm token; "24" → "09:05" / "21:05" (two-digit hour, no am/pm). Default "12". (The table always shows both forms.)

analogue.description: TABLE only: include the analogue mini-dial column (a small reference clock face — ring and two hands, no numerals). False drops it for a purely digital 12-hr | 24-hr table. Default true.

arrow.description: TABLE only: draw the derived link between the 12-hour and 24-hour cells showing the hour change ("+12" for pm times, "−12" for midnight, "same" for am times and noon). Default true.

stem.description: Show the warm verbal stem sentence — the spoken twin of the figure (READOUT: "13:07 is the same as 1:07 pm, in the afternoon"; TABLE: the conversion rule). It is automatically suppressed whenever a segment or cell is occluded, so it can never leak an answer. Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
